items.title: Cuddlers help babies
items.text: For over 35 years, Rush University Medical Center in Chicago, USA, has been helping infant patients and their families through a volunteer cuddler program. When families are away from the hospital’s neonatal intensive care unit (NICU), volunteers comfort infants with cuddles. Families can’t be in the hospital all the time, but the babies had needs after they left. The staff understood these needs, and volunteer cuddlers helped. A lot of the volunteers are parents whose children were in the NICU before. After undergoing extensive training, they are using their experiences and skills to provide other parents a sense of relief and security. Studies show that interactions like holding, rocking, singing, reading, and talking to the infants reduce stress and pain, and they improve their overall physical health. Difficult words: infant (a very young child), neonatal (newborn children), comfort (to make someone feel better). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: Cuddlers help babies
items.text: More than 35 years ago, workers at a medical center in Chicago, USA, thought about how they could help babies. Parents were sad at the hospital’s neonatal intensive care unit . They couldn’t be with their babies all the time. The hospital staff knew that babies needed someone’s care when their parents weren’t there. The children felt better and they were healthier when someone held them, sang, and talked to them. Volunteers took special training to learn how to cuddle the babies and make them feel better. Many of the volunteers were parents whose babies also spent time at the unit. Thanks to the volunteers, other parents didn’t feel guilty when they had to leave because they knew that someone else helped their child. Difficult words: neonatal intensive care unit (a special area of the hospital where staff look after newborn babies), volunteer (a person who does work for no money), guilty (when a person feels bad that he did something wrong). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Cuddlers help babies
items.text: A neonatal intensive care unit is a place in the hospital. Very young babies are there. The staff must look after them all the time. Parents stay with the children, too. They cannot be there all the time. They feel bad about it. The staff get an idea at a medical center in Chicago, USA. They start a volunteer cuddler program. This program starts 35 years ago. People in this program get special training. They learn how to cuddle babies. They learn how to make them feel good. Many of the volunteers are parents. Volunteers cuddle the babies. They sing and talk to them. Studies show that these babies feel better. They are healthier. Their parents feel better, too. Their children are not alone. Difficult words: staff (all the people who work in one organization), volunteer (a person who works for no money), cuddle (to hold someone for a long time in a loving way). items.title: COP31 brings no deal
items.text: The United Nations COP31 climate talks in Turkey failed to reach a major new agreement to tackle global warming. Although negotiations were extended late into Sunday, which made it the longest UN climate conference in history, deep divisions over fossil fuels and financial aid prevented a deal. The EU, the UK, and vulnerable Pacific island nations rejected the final draft text because oil-producing countries blocked any mention of transitioning away from fossil fuels, the primary driver of climate change. At the same time, African and developing nations objected to the lack of clear financial commitments from wealthy countries to help them adapt to extreme weather and rising sea levels. Conference leaders and campaigners warned that the collapse represents a serious blow to global cooperation, and urged wealthy nations to show stronger leadership, limit the influence of fossil fuel lobbyists , and deliver real climate finance. Difficult words: vulnerable (likely to be harmed, damaged, or negatively affected), primary driver (the most important factor or force that causes something to happen or develop), lobbyist (a person who takes part in an organized attempt to influence legislators or officials to support a particular interest or industry). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: COP31 brings no deal
items.text: COP31, the United Nations climate conference in Turkey, ended without a new agreement because countries couldn’t agree on fossil fuels and money. The meeting lasted longer than any previous climate conference as leaders tried to find a solution . The EU, the UK, and small island nations refused to accept the final plan because it didn’t mention stopping the use of fossil fuels, which causes global warming. At the same time, poorer countries in Africa and elsewhere were angry because rich nations didn’t promise enough money to help them deal with floods, heat waves, and rising oceans. Many experts and activists said the failed talks are a big problem for the world and asked rich countries to take stronger action against climate change. Difficult words: previous (the one before now), solution (the way of solving a problem or dealing with a difficult situation), refuse (to say no). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: COP31 brings no deal
items.text: There is a big United Nations meeting about climate change in Turkey. It is called COP31. It ends with no deal. Leaders from many countries talk for many days. But they can not agree . European countries and small island nations say no to the final plan . It does not talk about stopping oil, gas, and coal, which make the Earth warmer. Poorer countries are also unhappy. Rich countries do not promise money to help them with bad weather and rising seas. Many people are disappointed . They say that world leaders must work harder to save our planet and help poor nations. Difficult words: agree (to have the same idea; to say yes), final plan (the last version of a deal), disappointed (sad because something does not happen the way you wish). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Governments asking people to prep for emergencies
items.text: European governments are asking people to prepare for emergencies by keeping enough food and water to survive for 72 hours. The UK, France, Ireland, and the Netherlands have provided information to encourage people to prepare for possible disasters. The UK's campaign has a simple name. It is called "Be Ready". It advises families to store bottled water, canned food, a wind-up radio, and sleeping bags. The advice is changing people's shopping habits. Sales of bottled water in the UK have risen by 67 per cent, while sales of canned food have increased by 37 per cent. A London shop owner said: "There is an uplift, 100 per cent." He said he is selling a lot of torches and camping cookers. Governments are worried that events could stop people from getting things they need. These events include extreme weather, like heatwaves, storms, and wildfires. In addition, cyberattacks could affect supermarkets, electricity networks, and other important services. Recently, cyberattacks on European supermarkets caused problems with refrigerators and freezers. Stores had to throw away large amounts of frozen and chilled food. Other events, such as computer system failures, could also stop people using the internet or accessing cash. The UK government said people should take "simple steps" to be ready. items.title: U.S. brings an end to production of one-cent coin
items.text: The United States has officially brought an end to the production of its one-cent coin. President Donald Trump signed the Common Cents Act on Friday. However, the coin will remain legal tender and continue circulating. The US Mint had actually stopped manufacturing the penny (the nickname for the coin) in November 2025. Businesses now have to round cash transactions up or down to the nearest five cents when exact change is unavailable. The decision to discontinue minting the penny was an economic one. In 2024, each coin cost 3.69 cents to produce. The bill's author, Lisa McClain, said: "This legislation will save $85 million per year by permanently ending penny production. It's common sense." The penny's history dates back to the founding years of the United States. Congress established the US Mint in 1792. The following year, the mint distributed more than 11,000 one-cent coins. The penny underwent numerous design changes. Early designs included an image of Liberty, a Native American chief's headdress, and an eagle. In 1909, it featured a portrait of former President Abraham Lincoln to commemorate the centenary of his birth. The last major redesign was in 2010. Rising manufacturing costs gradually undermined the coin's viability, consigning it to history. Wikipedia stated that the coin was eventually "viewed as a burden to businesses, banks, government, and the public". Buy my 1,000 Ideas and Activities for Language Teachers eBook. items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 is released worldwide
items.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) has finally been released. Millions of video game fans worldwide are now playing it. They have waited 13 years for a new GTA game since the release of GTA 5. Gaming experts say the latest version could be the biggest entertainment release in history. It has already sold millions of copies, and it is set to make billions of dollars. Some fans are so excited that they are taking days off work or school to play it. An HR company in the UK said that workers in Britain booked around 83,000 days off because of the game. Many fans tried to make their games consoles think they lived in New Zealand by changing their region settings. They tried this so they could play the game earlier. GTA 6 has received excellent reviews for its high-quality, realistic graphics and exciting story. Players get to explore a huge world of crime and follow the lives of two criminals. However, many experts warn that the game is unsuitable for children under the age of 17. That is because it contains violence, killing, car theft, bad language, drugs, alcohol and sexual content. Media expert Jasmine Hood Miller said: "In GTA, players commit crimes, sometimes against ordinary people who did nothing wrong." She added: "GTA is a very well-made game that teens find fun to play." items.title: Wire upgrade at fault for grounding all US flights
items.text: Thousands of flights across the USA were grounded on Friday the 13th following a major communications failure in the country's air traffic control system. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop after problems with radar and communications equipment. More than 3,500 airplanes were in the air at the time. Thousands of flights were cancelled, leaving passengers stranded at airports nationwide. The problem was eventually traced to an overloaded router, possibly as a result of maintenance work to replace decades-old copper wires with fibre-optic cables. The FAA lifted the ground stop almost five hours later. Operations may take days to return to normal. The incident sparked widespread concern. Officials quickly reassured the public that it was not another 9/11. The US homeland security secretary said there had been no indication of a cyberattack or national security threat. He described the incident as a "telecommunications outage". Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed the failure on outdated infrastructure. He said: "We have old switches and old routers. We use 1980s little copper lines." He added: "It's an old system that went down. It went down everywhere. It got overloaded." Duffy warned that systems would "continue to break" unless Congress allocated extra funds. He said: "I can't build things if I don't have money." items.title: Trump calls Putin his friend
items.text: US President Donald Trump is defending his recent trilateral summit in China with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, even though the high-profile meeting produced few concrete results and left American allies unsettled . At a news conference on Friday, Trump described Putin as his friend and insisted that their personal relationship could help end Russia’s ongoing war in Ukraine. However, Trump declined to say whether Putin acts as a friend to American interests. He stated that ending the conflict is extremely difficult and blamed both sides for not knowing how to stop it. Shortly after the summit, Trump also called into a meeting of European leaders and reportedly questioned their continued support for Ukraine, right as fresh Russian strikes damaged European embassies in Kyiv. Despite Trump’s claims of progress, analysts note that Putin has shown no sign of wanting peace and no peace deal is any closer. Difficult words: trilateral (involving three groups, parties, or countries), unsettled (anxious, uneasy, or worried about a situation), decline (to refuse to accept, do, or answer something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: Trump calls Putin his friend
items.text: US President Donald Trump is defending his recent meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in China. Although the meeting brought together the world’s three biggest powers, it achieved very few real results and worried America’s European allies . At a news conference on Friday, Trump called Putin his friend and said their good relationship could help stop the war in Ukraine. Trump could not say if Putin is a friend to the United States, though. Soon after the meeting, Trump spoke to European leaders and questioned why they continue to support Ukraine, even as new Russian attacks hit buildings in Kyiv. Critics point out that Putin started the invasion and shows no real signs of stopping the war, which means Trump is still far from making a peace deal. Difficult words: ally (a country or organization that formally cooperates with and supports another, especially in politics or war), question (to express doubt about something, or to ask someone questions to get information), invasion (coming to a country or region with an armed force). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Trump calls Putin his friend
items.text: US President Donald Trump meets with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in China. The big meeting does not bring many real results . It makes America’s friends in Europe feel worried. On Friday, Trump calls Putin his friend. He says that their good relationship can help end the war in Ukraine. But Trump does not say if Putin is good for America. Later, Trump talks to European leaders. He asks why they still help Ukraine. At the same time, Russia attacks Kyiv again. Many people say that Putin does not want to stop fighting. There is still no peace deal . Difficult words: result (how a situation ends), relationship (how two or more people, groups, or countries behave toward each other), peace deal (a formal deal between countries to stop fighting). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Runners and cyclists make art
items.text: Fitness fanatics are creating art while tracking their runs and bike rides on their phones, turning their exercise into a masterpiece. When you create art with your GPS as a paintbrush, you follow points on a map to make a single line across an area to create the art. You enter the points into a fitness tracking app called Strava in advance , and the app then traces your every move. If you make a mistake, your whole artwork has to be started all over again. Artists from around the world upload their drawings to Instagram, where they join a growing gallery with more than 18,000 pieces posted under the hashtag GPS Art that already show hundreds of thousands of kilometers. Artists say that the activity is a mix of art and exercise, and for many, it began with the pandemic when traffic suddenly went away and people had more free time. Difficult words: fanatic (a person who’s extremely interested in something), in advance (before doing a particular thing), hashtag (the symbol # that’s used on social media to describe the general subject). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: Runners and cyclists make art
items.text: During the coronavirus pandemic, there were fewer cars on the roads, and people had more free time, too. Some runners and cyclists started to create new and unusual art. Strava is a GPS cycling and running app, and some people started to use it as a paintbrush to create art. They entered some points in the app, and then they followed the points to make a line from them. Cyclists sometimes went tens of kilometers because if they made a mistake, they had to start all over again. The result is amazing. People make symbols, pictures, or even messages which they can share with other people on social media. One Instagram gallery already had more than 18,000 pieces of art, and people from all the world add theirs every day. Many people enjoyed this activity because it was a good way to exercise and create art at the same time. Difficult words: GPS (an electronic system which uses satellites to tell where exactly someone or something is), enter (to put data or information into a computer), gallery (a place where people see and sometimes can buy works of art). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Runners and cyclists make art
items.text: Some runners and cyclists have a new hobby . They make special art . Fewer cars are on the roads during the coronavirus. People also have more free time. Some people make pictures. They use the Strava app . Strava is a cycling and running app. It shows where someone runs or cycles. Some people plan where they go. They put points in the app. Then they run or cycle. They connect the points. They make a picture from the points. They must start again if they make a mistake. One gallery on the Internet already has more than 18,000 pictures. People from all the world put the pictures there. There are new pictures every day. Difficult words: hobby (an activity which someone does in his free time for fun), art (paintings, drawings, music, and so on), app (a computer program in a mobile phone which does special things), gallery (a place to show art). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: France blames Iran for cyberattack on freezers
items.text: The French government has blamed Iran for a cyberattack on supermarket freezers and refrigerators across France. The attacks happened last month. They hit around 700 supermarkets and shops. Hackers took control of the cooling systems in the fridges and freezers. Temperatures increased to more than 50 degrees Celsius. Thousands of tons of frozen food melted. Stores had to throw the food away because it was no longer safe to eat. The French Foreign Minister said the attack was on a level never seen before. France believes an Iranian cyber unit carried out the attack. Iran has strongly denied it was involved in the attacks and blamed the French government for them. Security experts have warned that cyberattacks could be more dangerous in the future. Similar attacks have already affected other European countries. A French blood bank has also been hit. Fortunately, workers stopped the blood products from being damaged. Cybersecurity expert Gerome Billois stated: "At the moment, they are attacking easy equipment, but we should be prepared to see attacks on other systems like water or electricity." Weak computer security can let hackers attack places and services, such as hospitals, airports, public transport and banks. This can put people's lives in danger. items.title: Oil pollution in the sea
items.text: Severe oil pollution from damaged ships during the conflict involving Iran is threatening marine life and coastal communities across the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz. According to the International Maritime Organization, 136 maritime incidents have been confirmed in the region, while Greenpeace reports that satellite monitoring has detected more than 500 oil slicks since the war began. One recently spotted slick covers around 300 square kilometers, including a thick, dark section of heavy oil. Environmental experts warn that because the Gulf consists of shallow, semi-enclosed waters with limited exchange with the open ocean, trapped oil can remain in the environment for years. The spills have already washed onto coastlines in Iran, Oman, and the United Arab Emirates, and some beaches had to be closed temporarily. Conservationists are deeply concerned about vulnerable marine habitats , coral reefs, and rare species such as sea turtles and the endangered Arabian Sea humpback whale. Difficult words: slick (a film or layer of oil floating on water, especially one that has leaked from a ship), semi-enclosed (partially surrounded or shut in by land or barriers, limiting connection to the open sea), habitat (the natural home or environment of an animal, plant, or other organism).
